title: Pullback along an equivalence over an isofibration is an equivalence
statement: Use quasicategories, functor equivalences and degreewise simplicial pullbacks as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and isofibrations as defined in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Fix a universe containing the quasicategories $A,B,C$. Let $y:A\to B$ be a functor equivalence and $\pi:C\to B$ an isofibration. Form $E=A\times_B C$, with projections $s:E\to A$ and $r:E\to C$. Then $E$ is a quasicategory and $r$ is a functor equivalence. The identity $\pi r=ys$ holds as simplicial maps. No isofibration hypothesis on $y$ and no nonemptiness hypothesis on $E$ is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, category-of-elements proof: pullback of the representable subcategory along the Yoneda equivalence and the resulting equivalence of total categories; read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Unfold the degreewise pullback from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: an $n$-simplex of $E$ is $(a,c)$ with $y(a)=\pi(c)$, and operators act on both coordinates. Thus $\pi r=ys$ exactly. Given an inner horn in $E$, fill its $A$ coordinate to $a:\Delta^n\to A$. The $C$ coordinate of the horn and the bottom simplex $ya$ form an inner-horn lifting problem for $\pi$. The inner-fibration condition in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] supplies $c:\Delta^n\to C$ with $\pi c=ya$. The pair $(a,c)$ fills the original horn, so $E$ is a quasicategory. This conditional construction requires no vertex of $E$ when no horn map exists.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.28, quasicategory condition expanded directly from inner-horn lifting.

proof.text: Fix any small quasicategory $Q$ in the chosen universe. Write $F_X=\operatorname{Fun}(Q,X)$ for $X=A,B,C,E$. The identity of a quasicategory is an isofibration: the bottom simplex or equivalence edge is itself a filler. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] with the inclusion $\varnothing\hookrightarrow Q$ and each identity map. Since $\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,X)=\Delta^0$, this proves that every $F_X$ is a quasicategory. Its terminal map $F_X\to\Delta^0$ is an isofibration: fill inner horns in $F_X$ and lift the constant equivalence by an identity edge. Therefore [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration] makes $F_X^\simeq$ Kan. Put $U=F_A^\simeq$, $G=F_B^\simeq$, $V=F_C^\simeq$, and $J=F_E^\simeq$. Postcomposition induces simplicial maps $Y:U\to G$, $v:V\to G$, and $\rho_Q:J\to V$. Simplicial maps preserve equivalence edges because they preserve their inverses and both witness triangles.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.3.7 applied to the terminal maps of the functor quasicategories; exponential construction as in the existing exponentiation node.

proof.text: Choose the quasi-inverse $z:B\to A$ and coherent natural equivalences $\eta:zy\simeq\operatorname{id}_A$, $\epsilon:yz\simeq\operatorname{id}_B$ supplied by the hypothesis on $y$, using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Postcomposition by $y,z$ gives maps $Y_0:F_A\to F_B$, $Z_0:F_B\to F_A$. Whiskering $\eta$ gives a homotopy $Z_0Y_0\to\operatorname{id}_{F_A}$: evaluated on $(f,q,t)$ it is $\eta(f(q),t)$. This is simplicial since evaluation and composition commute with every operator. More explicitly, the simplicial map $\operatorname{Fun}(A,A)\to\operatorname{Fun}(F_A,F_A)$ sends an $n$-simplex $a:A\times\Delta^n\to A$ to $(f,t)\mapsto(q\mapsto a(f(q),t))$. It sends the chosen inverse edge and the two witness triangles for $\eta$ to such witnesses for its whiskering. Whiskering $\epsilon$ by the identical construction gives an equivalence edge $Y_0Z_0\simeq\operatorname{id}_{F_B}$. Thus these are actual coherent equivalences, including their inverse witnesses.

source.place: Elementary evaluation/whiskering expansion of coherent natural equivalences; compare Theorem 4.4.4.4, without using its converse.

proof.text: The homotopies in Step 3 restrict to simplicial homotopies on $U$ and $G$. Here is the edge check for the first one. Its component at a vertex $f$ is an equivalence, by applying evaluation at $f$ to its inverse witnesses. An edge of $U\times\Delta^1$ either stays at one endpoint or goes from $(f,0)$ to $(f',1)$ along an equivalence $a:f\to f'$ in $U$. In the latter case the triangle with vertices $(f,0),(f',0),(f',1)$ shows that its image has class $[\eta_Q(f')]\,[Z_0Y_0(a)]$ in $hF_A$. Both factors are invertible. By [lem-coef-homotopy-category-triangle-calculus], an inverse class is represented by an edge and its two inverse equalities have triangle witnesses. Hence the image edge is an equivalence. Every edge of every image simplex is therefore an equivalence, so that simplex lies in the core by definition. The same check with $F_B$ and $\epsilon_Q$ treats the other homotopy. Postcomposition by $z$ also preserves cores. Consequently $Y:U\to G$ has a simplicial homotopy inverse; [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] makes $Y$ a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13, forward implication; the restriction to cores is the explicit triangle calculation here.

proof.text: Use the path-space model $P(u,w)$ for a homotopy pullback specified in [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance]. Compare the cospans $U\xrightarrow{Y}G\xleftarrow{v}V$ and $G\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}G\xleftarrow{v}V$ by vertical maps $Y,\operatorname{id}_G,\operatorname{id}_V$. Their squares commute exactly, all objects are Kan by Step 2, and all vertical maps are weak homotopy equivalences by Step 4 or are identities. That node gives a weak homotopy equivalence $a:P(Y,v)\to P(\operatorname{id}_G,v)$, with formula $(u,w,\gamma)\mapsto(Yu,w,\gamma)$. In particular this map preserves the $V$ coordinate.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.9, applied with the middle and right vertical maps identities; path model Construction 3.4.0.3 (010B).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] to $\pi:C\to B$ and $y:A\to B$. It gives a weak homotopy equivalence $c:J\to P(Y,v)$ whose path coordinate is constant. Also [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], applied to $\operatorname{id}_G:G\to G$ and $v:V\to G$, gives a weak homotopy equivalence $j:V\to P(\operatorname{id}_G,v)$, $w\mapsto(vw,w,\operatorname{const}_{vw})$. Its fibration hypothesis holds because the identity lifts every horn. Let $p:P(\operatorname{id}_G,v)\to V$ forget the first and path coordinates. The formula gives $pj=\operatorname{id}_V$ and $pac=\rho_Q$ as exact simplicial equalities. The model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] has the realization weak homotopy equivalences as its weak equivalences; its model axioms give composition and two-out-of-three. From $j$ and $pj=\operatorname{id}$ it follows that $p$ is weak, and then $pac=\rho_Q$ is weak. This proves the assertion for every $Q$ about the specified postcomposition map.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.28 and the constant-path comparison, followed by composition and two-out-of-three for weak homotopy equivalences.

proof.text: Take $Q=C$ in Step 6. Its map $\rho_C:F_E^\simeq\to F_C^\simeq$ is a weak homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. By [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse], choose a simplicial inverse $b_C$ with the two simplicial homotopies in that statement. The vertex $t=b_C(\operatorname{id}_C)$ is an actual simplicial functor $C\to E$. Evaluating the homotopy $\rho_C b_C\to\operatorname{id}$ at $\operatorname{id}_C$ gives an edge $\alpha:rt\to\operatorname{id}_C$ in the core of $\operatorname{Fun}(C,C)$. Every core edge is an equivalence in that functor quasicategory, so $\alpha$ is a coherent natural equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13, converse, evaluated at the identity functor; this is the first half of the explicit inverse-detection argument.

proof.text: Take $Q=E$ in Step 6 and apply [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse] to obtain $b_E:V\to J$ and a homotopy $b_E\rho_E\to\operatorname{id}_J$, now with $J=\operatorname{Fun}(E,E)^\simeq$, $V=\operatorname{Fun}(E,C)^\simeq$. Precomposing $\alpha$ from Step 7 with $r$ gives an equivalence edge $rtr\to r$ in $V$: precomposition sends both inverse witnesses to inverse witnesses. Applying $b_E$ gives an edge $b_E(rtr)\to b_E(r)$ in $J$. Evaluating the homotopy at $tr$ and $\operatorname{id}_E$ gives edges $b_E(rtr)\to tr$ and $b_E(r)\to\operatorname{id}_E$ in $J$. These three edges are equivalences in $\operatorname{Fun}(E,E)$. Compose their classes, reversing the first of the latter two edges, to obtain an isomorphism $tr\to\operatorname{id}_E$ in its homotopy category. By [lem-coef-homotopy-category-triangle-calculus] this class and its inverse have edge representatives and both inverse equations have triangle witnesses. Thus $tr\simeq\operatorname{id}_E$ coherently. Together with $rt\simeq\operatorname{id}_C$ this makes $r$ a functor equivalence as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. All the arguments apply when any category is empty; Whitehead and the definitions impose no nonemptiness condition.

source.place: Agent-expanded second half of inverse detection from the core tests, using Proposition 3.1.7.13; no uncited infinity-categorical Yoneda theorem is invoked.
